title: Ferns Behind Glass
paras: In nineteenth-century Britain, a growing [[liking|liking]] for ferns brought woodland plants into city homes. Yet keeping them alive was difficult: coal smoke polluted the air, while indoor fires dried it. A solution emerged in 1829, when a London doctor noticed a fern growing inside a closed glass container originally used to observe an insect.

The container offered a [[glimpse|glimpse]] of a miniature water cycle. Moisture rose from the soil, collected on the glass and returned as drops. Glass walls could [[restrict|restrict]] exposure to dirty air without blocking daylight. The fern, an [[inhabitant|inhabitant]] of damp, sheltered places, could therefore survive with little watering. These containers became known as Wardian cases, after the doctor who developed them.

By the middle of the century, glass cases had become fashionable household objects. A [[decorator|decorator]] could place one beside a window, making its wooden frame part of a room's design. Arranging rocks and leaves became an [[artistic|artistic]] activity, turning a small box into a green [[paradise|paradise]]. At horticultural exhibitions, a [[contestant|contestant]] might display carefully cultivated ferns rather than flowering plants. Their delicate shapes offered a different kind of beauty.

The fashion also had a darker side. Collectors sometimes removed whole plants from woodland, leaving a [[heap|heap]] of disturbed earth behind. As observers became more [[conscious|conscious]] of this damage, enthusiasm for collecting increasingly faced criticism. Although the Victorian craze eventually faded, its glass gardens helped establish a lasting idea: successful plant care begins with understanding the conditions a plant needs.
zh: 在十九世纪的英国，人们对蕨类植物日益浓厚的喜爱，使这些林地植物进入了城市家庭。然而，要让它们存活并不容易：煤烟污染了空气，室内炉火又使空气变得干燥。1829年，一位伦敦医生发现，一个原本用于观察昆虫的密闭玻璃容器里长出了一株蕨类植物，由此找到了解决办法。
这个容器让人们得以窥见一个微型水循环。水分从土壤中蒸发，在玻璃上凝结，再化作水滴落下。玻璃壁既能减少植物接触污浊空气的机会，又不会挡住日光。因此，原本生长在潮湿、避风环境中的蕨类植物，无须频繁浇水也能存活。这种容器后来以开发它的医生之名，被称为沃德箱。
到了十九世纪中叶，玻璃植物箱已成为时髦的家居用品。室内装饰师可以将它摆在窗边，让木制框架融入房间的设计。摆放石块和叶片成了一种艺术活动，把小箱子变成一片绿色乐园。在园艺展览上，参赛者可能会展示精心培育的蕨类植物，而非开花植物。它们纤巧的形态呈现出另一种美。
这股风潮也有其阴暗面。采集者有时会从林地中挖走整株植物，只留下一堆翻动过的泥土。随着人们逐渐意识到这种破坏，热衷采集植物的行为受到了越来越多的批评。虽然维多利亚时代的这股热潮最终消退了，但这些玻璃花园帮助确立了一个长久适用的理念：成功养护植物，始于了解它所需要的生长条件。

q.s: The doctor had kept the insect in the container for several weeks before noticing the fern.
q.why: 未说明发现蕨类前昆虫已在容器中多久。

q.s: Ferns in Wardian cases could survive with little watering.
q.why: 第二段明确说蕨类只需少量浇水即可存活。

q.s: Collectors always left whole fern plants in place in the woodland.
q.why: 末段说采集者有时会挖走整株植物。
